proof_audit.claim: Finite posterior, predictive dependence and Bayes action
proof_audit.argument: Normalize prior times likelihood only when the marginal is positive. Conditional binary future records are integrated over the posterior; their joint success probability is the second parameter moment and covariance is posterior parameter variance. Explicit utility 3 for the high state and -2 otherwise yields threshold 2/5. The alternative proper prior changes the action.
proof_audit.hypotheses: Proper finite prior, likelihood for the specified ordered three-success/one-failure record, conditional iid future Bernoulli draws and the stated utility.
proof_audit.limits: Conditional posterior probability is not a frequentist coverage or causal identification theorem.

proof_audit.claim: Finite Hastings flow, invariance, minorization, TV convergence and stationary uniqueness
proof_audit.argument: Off-diagonal accepted flows equal the minimum of forward/reverse target-proposal flows, including zero reverse support. Diagonals retain rejected/self proposals. Summing balance yields invariance. P=delta Pi+(1-delta)R with R stochastic gives TV contraction by the triangle inequality; comparison with the invariant target yields uniqueness and convergence. Delta=1 is the iid-target case.
proof_audit.hypotheses: Finite positive target, stochastic proposal, explicit acceptance and 0<delta<=1 minorization for the convergence claim.
proof_audit.limits: Invariance alone permits a periodic example; no generic state-space ergodic or CLT theorem is claimed.

proof_audit.claim: Exact covariance law, average variance and L2 law for the selected observable; separate low-start mean
proof_audit.argument: The centered high-state indicator is an eigenfunction with lambda=50/81. Iterated conditional expectations under stationarity give gamma_k=gamma_0 lambda^k. Expanding the sum counts n-k covariance pairs, yielding exact n=4 variance. Geometric domination bounds n times the variance and controls its tail for the limit. Low-start means instead follow the initial eigenfunction value and are checked by state-law multiplication; that initial run does not inherit stationary finite covariance.
proof_audit.hypotheses: Stationary initialization for covariance/variance; separately stipulated low initialization for its bias; 0<lambda<1 for the nonnegative geometric bound used.
proof_audit.limits: No Markov-chain CLT, arbitrary effective sample-size formula or estimated long-run variance consistency is proved.

proof_audit.claim: Attainment, necessary and sufficient KKT, orthogonal soft threshold and fit uniqueness
proof_audit.argument: Positive lambda makes sublevel sets compact through the l1 norm. Nonzero coordinate derivatives and both one-sided zero-coordinate derivatives give the exact score conditions. A chosen l1 subgradient plus convexity proves sufficiency. Orthonormal Gram completes squares and separates scalar minimizations. Strict convexity in fitted values and convexity of the penalty rule out two distinct optimal fits by a midpoint argument.
proof_audit.hypotheses: Fixed finite X,y, loss ||y-Xb||^2/(2n)+lambda||b||1, lambda>0 and every coefficient penalized, including the constant column.
proof_audit.limits: Coefficient uniqueness requires more than fit uniqueness; the orthogonal numerical solver is not applied to general X.

proof_audit.claim: Sparse event-conditional bounds with explicit constants and separate Gaussian event probability
proof_audit.argument: Comparing to the exact-sparse reference and cancelling the noise square yields the basic inequality. Dual Holder with score norm <=lambda/2 and support decomposition gives prediction/(2n)+(lambda/2)||Delta_Sc||1 <=(3lambda/2)||Delta_S||1. This implies the cone. The stated full-vector unsquared curvature supplies kappa^2||Delta||2^2 <=3lambda sqrt(s)||Delta||2; zero error is handled separately. Substitution and the cone give coefficient l2, prediction and l1 bounds. Gaussian mgf/Chernoff gives each score tail and a union bound gives the tuning value without score independence.
proof_audit.hypotheses: Exact support s>=1, noise event, and ||Xv||/sqrt(n)>=kappa||v||2 for every cone vector, kappa>0. The separate probability result assumes fixed column norms <=sqrt(n), iid Gaussian errors with positive variance.
proof_audit.limits: No support-only norm substitution, arbitrary random-design curvature, support recovery, adaptive-lambda theorem or post-selection inference. Source display constants were not copied.

proof_audit.claim: Entire unweighted minimizer set and weighted unique selection
proof_audit.argument: Set t=b1+b2 and use |b1|+|b2|>=|t|. The reduced strict convex scalar optimum t=3/2 is attained only by nonnegative splits. The cone contains the null direction (a,-a), refuting positive full-vector curvature. With exact weights (1,2), |b1|+2|b2|>=|t|+|b2| makes the reduced lower bound attainable only with b2=0.
proof_audit.hypotheses: n=1, X=(1,1), y=2, lambda=1/2; weights (1,2) only in the transfer.
proof_audit.limits: Penalty asymmetry selects coefficients without supplying new data identification.

proof_audit.claim: Causal ATE identity, exact double-robust remainder and product norm bound
proof_audit.argument: Consistency/exchangeability/overlap identify m_d. Condition on X and collect regression errors to obtain (e-e0){(g1-m1)/e+(g0-m0)/(1-e)}. Correct propensity or both correct regressions suffice for zero mean bias; a both-wrong cancellation shows necessity does not follow. Bounded paths preserving overlap make the remainder second order, and Cauchy-Schwarz gives its L2 product bound. The oracle variance decomposes into conditional-effect variance plus conditional residual variance, with cross terms zero.
proof_audit.hypotheses: Specified potential-outcome iid construction, no interference, conditional independence of treatment, positivity; candidate propensity clipped away from endpoints for norm control.
proof_audit.limits: Predictive accuracy does not establish these identifying restrictions. One correct nuisance alone does not force the joint-truth influence variance.

proof_audit.claim: Bounded iid cross-fitted ATE root-N expansion
proof_audit.argument: Condition separately on one outside training sample and the independently chosen/fixed partition. Score-difference expansion bounds its L2 norm by b/c+2Ba/c^2. Exact mean is at most ab/c=o_p(N^-1/2). Conditional variance of the held-out mean is at most Pr^2/n_k. Conditional Chebyshev truncated at one tends to zero in probability; bounded splitting shows its expectation tends to zero, establishing unconditional negligible centered error. Repeat for fixed K and sum weighted errors without assuming fit independence. Apply only the inherited iid CLT to the oracle sum.
proof_audit.hypotheses: Fixed K>=2, n_k/N to positive fractions below one, all fitting/tuning/preprocessing outside the fold, bounded outcomes/regressions, true/fitted overlap, foldwise L2 consistency, sqrt(N)ab=o_p(1), positive finite oracle variance.
proof_audit.limits: No joint conditional iid assertion given all fits; no generic DML theorem, data-adaptive fold guarantee, growing-fold or dependent-data result.

proof_audit.claim: Consistency of pooled score variance and studentization
proof_audit.argument: Conditional Markov and the same bounded conditional-probability argument imply empirical squared score differences tend to zero foldwise and hence after fixed-K pooling. Cauchy-Schwarz bounds the difference of score second moments, using bounded actual/fitted scores. Oracle square LLN and estimate consistency yield Vhat to V. Positive V and Slutsky justify standard error sqrt(Vhat/N).
proof_audit.hypotheses: Exactly the bounded fixed-fold theorem conditions and iid oracle law.
proof_audit.limits: Asymptotic normal inference is not exact finite-table coverage or semiparametric efficiency.

proof_audit.claim: Actual finite-cell learner rates; insufficient quarter-rate sequence; conditional-population L2 leakage counterexample
proof_audit.argument: Each cell has mass >=1/8. Bounded cell numerator/denominator averages have root-n errors by Chebyshev; denominator is bounded below with probability tending to one. Centered ratio numerator yields root-n cell means, with exponentially unlikely empty-cell exceptions. Laplace terms are O(1/n), clipping is nonexpansive relative to truth, finite cells and fixed folds give the required product rate. The explicit joint-truth perturbation has scaled bias tending to 1/3 despite both O(N^-1/4) rates. A continuous independent identifier assigns zero fresh-population mass to finite training overwrites while own-row scoring collapses to zero.
proof_audit.hypotheses: The specific bounded finite law and learner, training sample sizes proportional to N, independent continuous identifiers for the leakage construction.
proof_audit.limits: No arbitrary learner rate or finite-sample coverage assertion; the quarter-rate example deliberately uses true nuisance functions to demonstrate a theoretical boundary.

proof_audit.claim: Exact rejection count with ties and independent super-uniform FDR bound
proof_audit.argument: Largest passing rank implies exactly R values at the inclusive threshold. Zeroing p_i cannot reduce R. If i was rejected, ranks above R are unchanged, so R_i=R. Conversely if p_i<=qR_i/m, restoring it leaves at least R_i passing values, giving R>=R_i and equality. The indicator identity follows. Condition on the full other-p vector; independence plus super-uniformity bounds each true-null contribution by q/m. Sum over true nulls.
proof_audit.hypotheses: Fixed family and q in (0,1); each true-null p-value is independent of the entire vector of all other p-values and is super-uniform. False-null values may depend among themselves.
proof_audit.limits: The proof extends to discrete valid nulls independently of the original source uniform-order-statistics argument. It gives no arbitrary-dependence control.

proof_audit.claim: FDR, FWER and count-ratio distinction; exact dependence failure
proof_audit.argument: Complete 144-state law counts all R values and computes expected FDP directly. Each discrete null CDF is floor(12u)/12. In the four-state complete-null transfer, each marginal CDF meets super-uniformity at all jumps and between them, but BH rejects in three states with total mass 3/20. Bonferroni/Holm reject in two states with mass 1/10. Under a complete null a nonempty list always has FDP one.
proof_audit.hypotheses: The two separate fully specified finite joint laws, inclusive thresholds and FDP denominator max(R,1).
proof_audit.limits: Neither a controlled unconditional FDR nor marginal p-value validity controls every realized list; no uninspected dependence-extension theorem is claimed.
